Title: Diagnosis of test `testStopBursting`

Details:
The test `testStopBursting` is trying to parse the argument array `["-azc"]` using the command line parser, with the option `stopAtNonOption` set to true. According to the assertion in the test, after parsing, the command line's argument list size should be 1 (`cl.getArgList().size() == 1`).

from the snippet of `Parser.parse(Options, String[], boolean)` and `Parser.parse(Options, String[], Properties, boolean)`, we observe the parsing flow as follows:

- The parse method flattens the input arguments, then iterates through each token.
- It tracks a flag `eatTheRest` which becomes true if the parser encounters a non-option or an unknown option when `stopAtNonOption` is true.
- When this flag is set, the parser adds the rest of the tokens as arguments instead of options.
  
Specifically for the input `-azc` (a combined string of options), the parser should ideally split it into individual options `-a`, `-z`, `-c` and treat them accordingly. If `stopAtNonOption` is true, any unknown or non-option token encountered would cause the parser to stop option processing and treat the remaining as arguments.

The test expects that after parsing `-azc` with `stopAtNonOption` set true, the argument list should have 1 element, which probably means that bursting (splitting) of the combined option string has stopped and the remainder is treated as an argument.

The failure may be caused by the parser either not stopping option bursting as expected or the `eatTheRest` flag not being set correctly when it encounters a non-option within a burst token. It also depends how `processOption()` method handles this combined token based on known options in `options`, which isn't visible yet.

Next, I will check the `flatten()` method related to options and arguments to understand how `-azc` is split/flattened and the `processOption()` method to verify how each option token is processed during parsing.

I will look up `flatten` and `processOption` methods in `org.apache.commons.cli.Parser`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
